author: /root/transport_dependency_audit
head: 451ef43
scope: Servlet built-in abort listener wiring only; shared utility and core lifecycle integration have separate reviews.

findings.problem: The early timeout listener checks both exchange monitor and writeLock, but the late onAbort registration only increments a counter. Late callbacks are also required to run outside those locks.
findings.why_material: A synchronized ServletExchange.onAbort method delegating to the common utility can pass the early-abort lock assertions while invoking an already-aborted late listener under the exchange monitor. This can deadlock a late core callback even though its count is correct.
findings.required_correction: Use assertCallbackUnlocked(ex) in the late listener as well, record any failure in the existing AtomicReference, and assert it remains null after late registration and repeated abort. Keep the existing exactly-once counts and cleanup assertions.

checks_passed: Real Jetty timeout detects abort and exercises an early throwing Error plus a surviving listener, late registration, and repeated abort.
The actual client-reset test requires a later write to throw IOException without the caller explicitly aborting, then checks adapter cleanup and a notification.
The truncated request supplies Content-Length20 with one byte and half-closes the actual socket; the handler catches the real request-body read IOException without invoking abort.
Synchronous and deferred successful finish produce no abort notification, including late listener registration and an abort attempt after successful completion.
Forced stop and both late SSE drain exception classes retain fail-soft cleanup when listeners throw.
Outside-monitor and outside-writeLock checks are concrete in early timeout and actual read/write failure callbacks.
Recorded20 targeted tests have5 actual RED failures and15 existing GREEN controls; no expected-failure or ignored test is counted as feature completion.
No new dependencies or core lifecycle obligations were introduced in this review.
nonblocking_suggestion: In clientResetDuringLaterWrite..., assert abortNotifications before closed(ex) attempts another commit. This makes the detected-write-failure observation precede any extra operation on the terminal exchange.
next: Add the late-callback lock assertion, then request round2. Maximum3 rounds; stop on first PASS.
